items.rationale: A LEFT JOIN keeps every student from the left table, including students who do not have a matching enrollment. For those unmatched students, the enrollment columns contain NULL values.
An INNER JOIN includes only rows with matching records in both tables. Since exactly 3 students each have one enrollment, the result contains 3 rows. The 2 students without enrollments are excluded.

items.answer: An INNER JOIN returns only students who have matching enrollment records. A LEFT JOIN keeps all students, including those without enrollments, and shows NULL values for the unmatched enrollment columns.
accepted: INNER JOIN only includes matching rows, while LEFT JOIN includes all rows from the left table.
An INNER JOIN excludes students without enrollments, but a LEFT JOIN keeps them with NULL enrollment values.
LEFT JOIN preserves unmatched students, whereas INNER JOIN removes them from the results.
